## Intent
Hypothesis: 4× unrolling the branchy integration loop amortizes per-iteration overhead and exposes ILP for the partially vectorizable FP sections, improving throughput over scalar.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 68 B/p offers 32 hot bytes (47%) for loop 1 and 28 (41%) for loop 2 — over half each line is dead weight. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers, but branchy respawn calls `bl spawn` per death, breaking any stream. The 4× unroll strides 0x110 (272 B), spanning ~2 cachelines per iteration. Working set spills L1d at N≈963 and L2 at N≈61680; with 47% hot bytes, dead bandwidth compounds in DRAM.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p is flat across all N — at q=0.01 it ranges 7.1–7.9 with no sharp knee at either spill. The L1d→L2 transition (N≈963) shows a slight rise to 7.86 at N=2400, then recovers to 7.1–7.4 in DRAM. The L2→DRAM transition (N≈62000) shows no penalty — cost drops slightly (7.42→7.12). This flatness means the algo is not memory-bound: sequential stride suffices despite 47% hot bytes, and compute/branch overhead dominates. The dense grid resolves both transitions as non-events.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth peaks at 9.6 GB/s (q=0.01, N=62000) — 32% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling, 3.1× above the 2.274 ns/p floor. At q=0.5 it falls to 5.0 GB/s (17%). The algo is compute-bound at low q (compute 63–70%, backend 25–27%) and shifts to branch-bound: at q=0.5, branch_flush hits 37% while backend drops to 7%. Ratios vs baseline are ~1.0x everywhere — the unroll buys nothing. Vs the winner the gap widens with q: 1.66x at q=0.01 (N=10M) but 2.50x at q=0.5 — the winner (autovec at q=0.01, halide at q≥0.1) replaces branchy respawn with select-based logic.

## Assembly
Loop 1 is unrolled 4× (stride 0x110) with shallow vectorization: `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` for position, `ext.16b` for AoS shuffle, `ld1.s` for indexed velocity gather. The death check is scalar and branchy: `fcmp s0, s13` + `b.ge` to a respawn path calling `bl spawn` — non-inlined per death. The PRNG (`clz`, `ror`, `eor`, `bfi`) is fully scalar. Loop 3 uses `csel` for clamping but writes pixels via `strb` (×16). Only 36/663 instructions are vector (5.4%) — branchy respawn and scalar PRNG dominate, capping bandwidth at 32% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.98–1.05x of baseline at every N×q point: the 4× unroll cannot overcome the branchy `bl spawn` respawn and scalar PRNG. At q=0.01 the algo is 1.66x slower than the winner (7.23 ns/p, N=10M); at q=0.5, 2.50x slower (13.52 ns/p) — the winner vectorizes the death-free path and replaces branchy respawn with select-based logic, cutting branch_flush from 37% toward zero. The unroll adds bloat (342 insns/iter) without ILP gain because the `fcmp`→`b.ge`→`spawn` chain is serial per particle.
